explanation: Fires on a middle or later subword piece of a multi-token proper name or technical term (mingw, Caucasians, NetBSD, Magdalene, Percolation, TicTacToe, Appellee), and also on the opening quote or bracket of a string in code. The top examples share no clear meaning, and the weak examples are function words.

Fires on the participle or adjective-forming piece right after a hyphen or noun in a compound modifier such as X-flagged, resin-modified, Rh-catalyzed, 125I-labeled, HIV-infected, community-acquired or Isis-linked. It is strongest on '-catalyzed/-modified/-labeled/-infected/-linked' and weaker on other hyphenated pieces.

Fires on an inner piece of a long word that is split into several tokens, often in non-English text (French, German, Spanish, Portuguese) or in words broken by soft hyphens or capitals (med-itat-ion, poss-ibili-ty, ex-empl-ified, O P I N I O N). It is weak on whole words and code.

Fires on the second or later token of a multi-word proper name or fixed phrase that the earlier tokens predict: vitamin K/E, Venice Biennale, Jackson Hole, Redwood Shores, American College, pretty much, HKEY_LOCAL. It responds to the token completing a known named entity or collocation.

Fires on a token that starts a placeholder or variable-like phrase in technical or form text: 'your'/'their'/'the' after a description or parameter dash, field names in code (user_id, Role, db.sql), and 'which'. It is mostly found in code docs, form instructions and SQL/JSON.

Fires on a wide spread of content and function tokens in mid-sentence (of, offset, tend, caused, lightweight, override, COPYING, continues, representation) that share no visible theme. Neither the token nor its context explains the pattern.

Fires on mixed tokens: completions of compound names (CoinDesk, linux/kernel, VrMath, Chem. Commun), word pieces in Danish, Finnish and Hungarian, and 'make' in 'how to make' or 'supposed to make'. There is no single theme.

Fires on assorted tokens right after a sentence's subject or clause opening (generally, and, starts, great, it, bold, started, that, joined, further). It is roughly a predicate or modifier position, but no consistent feature is visible.

Fires on the word that ends a fixed boilerplate phrase or names a field. The clearest case is 'permission' in 'without specific prior written permission' in BSD license headers. It also fires on filename extensions, identifiers in code strings, and the last word of fixed phrases.

Fires on verbs of changing, replacing or switching: change, changed, switching, replace, replaced, remove, relocating, restore, and Russian 'zamenit'. It is strongest when the verb means altering a name, plan or setting, and moderate on related verbs such as split, update or replacing.

Fires on a piece in the middle or end of the name of a US sports team, school, organisation or place, especially in sports and college contexts (Kansas City Athletics, UNC Pembroke, Kappa Delta Rho, NCAA Division, Southwest Atlanta Christian, Vuelta). It also fires on parts of other compound names, such as code identifiers.

Fires on 'at' in 'at least' and on 'minimum' (or 'a' in 'a minimum of') in phrases that set a lower bound or requirement. It is strongest on 'at' before 'least' after a requirement verb, and weaker on related limit words such as below, must, min or MAX.

Fires on mixed tokens: non-English word pieces (Danish, Finnish, Portuguese, Greek, CJK), 'is/and/are' in software license boilerplate, and the first piece of a split word (cum laude, double-stranded, hand-stitched). There is no clear unifying theme.

Fires on a heterogeneous set of tokens: pieces of all-caps words in legal captions (MEMORANDUM, JUDGMENT), 'of' in organisation names, code punctuation and keywords, and German word pieces. No single theme.

Fires on mixed tokens: the last digit of a season year range ('1968-69' in sports-season titles) and generic nouns for a thing being discussed in technical text (method, file, query, string, boot, migration). It also fires on chemistry word pieces.

Fires on a word-initial 'l'/'L' token or a short word starting with l/lo (l in 'sensu lato', L in LGA/Linq/LRB, lattes, lizards, luring, low, lofts). It responds to the letter-L opening of a word that is split into pieces.

Fires on an inner or later piece of a biomedical or scientific technical term (leukocyte antigen, interleukin, intercostal, interferon, tuberculin, somatostatin, dentate gyrus, adenosine), mostly in abstracts. A few code identifiers also fire.

Fires on a comma that ends an introductory or subordinate phrase in running prose, before the main or next clause. It also fires on 'era' in Diptera/viscera and on pieces of rare words (eviscerate, Accumbens).

Fires on the first piece of a capitalised proper name split into tokens, especially T and G (Troutman, Trenchardt, Graham, Ghetto, Gwyneth, GCHQ, Aeronautics). It is also moderate on the article 'a' before a noun phrase in narrative text.
Fires on a broad mixture of tokens (other, says, of in 'one of / 15% of', name in 'to name a few', un-needed, nearly, part) that share no visible feature.

Fires on words in the names of space agencies, missions and research organisations: Space(craft), Space Station, Cassini mission, Institute for Space Studies, Research, Energy. It is strongest in NASA or spaceflight contexts and moderate on 'research' and other science-institution words.
